  • Reporting & Steuerung: Aufbau eines klaren Marketing-Reportings (Kanal-Performance, CAC, ROAS, Retention) und laufende Auswertung von Traffic, Conversion und Nutzerverhalten – daraus leitest du Maßnahmen und Budgetallokation ab

Qualifikation

  • Mehrjährige, nachweisbare Erfahrung im E-Commerce- bzw. D2C-Marketing – idealerweise mit eigener Budgetverantwortung im Performance Marketing
  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse in Meta Ads und Google Ads sowie im Umgang mit Tracking- und Analyse-Tools (GA4, Google Tag Manager, Shopify-Reporting o. ä.)
  • Erfahrung mit E-Mail- und CRM-Tools (z. B. Klaviyo, chatarmin) sowie ein gutes Gespür für Zielgruppen, Segmentierung und Retention
  • Solides SEO-Verständnis und Neugier auf GEO – du beobachtest aktiv, wie sich Suche durch AI-Assistenten verändert
  • Aktive Nutzung von AI-Tools in der täglichen Arbeit und Freude daran, Prozesse damit neu zu denken
  • Grundkenntnisse in HTML, CSS und JavaScript sowie idealerweise erste Erfahrung mit Shopify (Theme-Anpassungen, Liquid, Apps)
  • Analytisches Denken, sicherer Umgang mit Zahlen und Excel/Google Sheets – Entscheidungen triffst du datenbasiert
  • Strukturierte, eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise mit ausgeprägter Hands-on-Mentalität – du konzipierst nicht nur, du setzt auch um
  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse, Englischkenntnisse auf mindestens B2-Niveau; Interesse an Darts ist kein Muss, hilft aber

Benefits

  • Jahresbruttogehalt zwischen 53.000 bis 58.000 Euro – je nach Qualifikation und Erfahrung
  • Volle Ownership für unterschiedliche Marketing Kanäle eines wachsenden D2C-Unternehmens mit gemeinsamen Media-Budget im siebenstelligen Bereich
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Gründern, kurze Entscheidungswege und großer Gestaltungsspielraum – neue Ideen werden getestet, nicht diskutiert
  • Hybrides Arbeiten möglich, Büro in Berlin-Charlottenburg mit sehr guter ÖPNV-Anbindung
  • Deutschlandticket als steuerfreies Jobticket
  • Monatlich eine Massage als steuerfreier Sachbezug
  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit Zuschuss vom Arbeitgeber
  • Kostenlose Getränke und Kaffee am Arbeitsplatz
  • Mitarbeiterrabatte auf unser gesamtes Sortiment

Spotify's mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by giving a million creative artists the opportunity to live off their art and billions of fans the chance to enjoy and be passionate about these creators.

The Subscriptions Mission builds and evolves Spotify's subscription products and marketplace experiences to drive sustainable user and revenue growth globally. We focus on awareness, acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization strategies that help users unlock the full value of Spotify while enabling the business to scale efficiently and responsibly.

This role focuses on the awareness, acquisition, and activation layers of the Subscriptions Mission, making Premium feel unmissable to free users long before a purchase decision. You'll own the strategy for how users discover, understand, and develop intent for Premium value, partnering closely with product, design, engineering, research, marketing, and data science to shape the moments, surfaces, and experiences that drive consideration across markets and segments.


What You Will Do
  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for how free users become aware of, experience, and develop intent for Premium, driving consideration, conversion intent, and subscriber growth across segments and markets.
  • Lead the discovery, design, and delivery of subscriber-facing features from early concept through global rollout.
  • Drive experiments that deepen our understanding of what makes users want Premium and measurably move free users closer to a purchase decision.
  • Turn behavioral, funnel, and market data into clear hypotheses, define meaningful success metrics, and build a prioritized experimentation roadmap.
  • Design rigorous A/B experiments to evaluate funnel changes against strong baselines, scaling approaches that demonstrably work across markets and segments.
  • Make pragmatic trade-offs across user value, revenue impact, regional nuance, and operational complexity, knowing when a simple flow change is enough and when a deeper platform capability is needed.
  • Partner with marketing, research, and regional teams to adapt value positioning and messaging for different markets, competitive landscapes, and user needs, including high-growth emerging markets where the path to Premium may look fundamentally different.
  • Communicate strategy, results, and trade-offs clearly to senior stakeholders, translating funnel mechanics and subscription economics into business impact and strategic direction.

    • Where You'll Be
  • You have a strong track record in product management and have shipped consumer-facing products or features at scale, with experience that translates well to subscription, marketplace, consumer growth, or media environments.
  • You have strong instincts for consumer value and what makes a product feel worth paying for, and understand how perception, positioning, and product experience work together to influence willingness to pay.
  • You can break down the path from awareness to conversion, identify the highest-leverage opportunities, and connect product decisions to downstream revenue outcomes such as ARPU, LTV, and net subscriber growth.
  • You're fluent in experimentation and A/B testing and are confident interpreting funnel, cohort, and behavioral analysis to make thoughtful prioritization decisions.
  • You know how to navigate the complexity of a global consumer business across different segments, markets, and competitive dynamics, balancing global consistency with local relevance.
  • You bring strong judgment about when to optimize, when to invest more deeply, and when to leave something alone, balancing user value, revenue impact, and operational cost.
  • You're a clear communicator and collaborative partner across product, design, engineering, marketing, research, data science, and regional teams, and you can align people around shared outcomes.

A Hybrid working model

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we've adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.

What does a Senior Account Manager do at WPP Production? 

As part of the Client Services Department, you play a central role in the business and are pivotal to the smooth running of your account. You will be required to have a thorough understanding of all areas of the business and be responsible for managing projects from brief to final delivery on time and budget. You will be client focused and require good communication, organisation and time management skills to manage both your clients and internal departments, while always focusing on quality, process and profitability. 

  

What does a Senior Account Manager do at WPP Production, on the TJX account? 

You will be working within the client's Activation Account team, implanted onsite working on behalf of the client. You will attend TJX office in Watford two/three times a week and occasionally work from the WPP Production office in London. You will deliver projects, working with TJX's onsite in-house creative team. You will be responsible for managing projects from briefing to final delivery, ensuring that TJX stakeholders, clients and agencies, adhere to set timings to ensure a timely delivery of all projects. You will be working on a range of Digital Media projects, such as Web, Email and Paid Media 

  

Client management responsibilities:  

  • Immerse yourself in the client's brand and offering

Reporting lines and key stakeholders 

This role reports to the Account Director, but you will have a dotted reporting line into a client lead (Brand Activation Manager. 

You will work closely with Creative, Digital and Production teams.

Do you want to lead the engineering functions that decide how a platform screening over a billion dollars of crypto transactions every week is built and run? Are you a DevOps leader fascinated by the possibilities of both agentic software solutions and the usage of agents in the software delivery lifecycle? Are you looking for a values-led company that cares about the growth of its people as much as the strength of its platform?

Elliptic is where ambitious people do the most important work of their careers. We are making crypto safe, secure and scalable, preventing global financial crime, exposing bad actors and protecting the world's financial system as it is being revolutionized. This is work your friends will actually want to hear about. You can expect to work in highly empowered teams, with remarkable breadth and the freedom to turn bold ideas into real impact, supported every step of the way by some of the most brilliant people you have ever called colleagues.

The impact you will have:

This role provides the people leadership for two connected functions at the heart of how Elliptic engineers. On the DevOps side, you keep a latency-sensitive screening platform dependable, cost-effective and scalable as transaction volume and customer expectations grow. On the AI Platform side, you lead the team that acts as Elliptic's centre of excellence for building AI agents, owning the shared frameworks, patterns, MCP management and evaluation capability that every product team draws on. You are a two-way conduit for that centre of excellence: carrying its best practice out to teams, and helping define what those best approaches should be. Reliability remains foundational to everything Elliptic does, and you will champion strong SRE practices across the business, though the SRE function itself sits outside your direct people-management scope. This is a hands-off, strategy and people-leadership role: you lead and grow the people, set the operating model, and make the calls that shape DevOps and AI Platform at Elliptic.

What you will do:

  • Lead, grow and develop the people across two functions, DevOps and AI Platform, owning hiring, levelling, coaching and career development for a combined team of roughly twelve engineers.

  • Set the strategy and operating model for DevOps: release safety, developer experience, observability, cost and the scalability of a latency-sensitive screening platform.

  • Lead the AI Platform function as a centre of excellence, owning the people and operating model behind Elliptic's shared agent-building frameworks and patterns, MCP management, evaluation framework and shared AI infrastructure.

  • Act as a two-way conduit for the centre of excellence: disseminate best practice and reusable approaches out to product teams building their own agents, and channel their feedback back to define and improve those approaches.

  • Partner with the AI Platform technical lead and senior engineers to shape technical direction, bringing people leadership and delivery rather than owning the technical vision single-handedly.

  • Own the cost, scalability and efficiency of the infrastructure as volume grows, bringing a FinOps mindset to infrastructure spend.

  • Champion SRE and reliability practices across the business, partnering closely with the SRE function.

  • Support the infrastructure and process maturity needed for certifications such as ISO 27001 and SOC2, working with InfoSec.

What you will achieve in the first 6 months:

  • Shaped and begun executing a people and hiring strategy across both functions, growing DevOps toward its target and building out the AI Platform and AI infrastructure team.

  • Begun operating as an effective conduit for the centre of excellence, strengthening how agent-building best practice, MCP and evaluation approaches are defined centrally and adopted by product teams.

  • Established a clear point of view on AI SDLC and how the platform enables it, and championed SRE practices across the business.

You will be a great fit here if you:

  • Lead through people: you measure your success by the growth and impact of your team, not your own output.

  • Are credible with senior engineers without needing to be the hands-on expert: you ask the sharp question and facilitate the right decision.

  • Are genuinely curious about AI, agents and evaluations, and energised by helping an organisation learn to build with them well.

  • Are honest and pragmatic about timelines and trade-offs, and comfortable owning a long-term build-out across two functions.

  • Care about the mission: providing the infrastructure and intelligence that keep financial institutions safe from crypto crime and sanctions evasion.

Our ideal candidate has:

  • A track record of managing DevOps, platform or infrastructure engineers, including hiring and building a growing team.

  • An infrastructure background (cloud, IaC, CI/CD, observability) deep enough to make sound strategic calls and guide senior engineers toward the right ones.

  • Extreme curiosity about AI and budding hands-on experience with AI, agents and evaluations: not necessarily deep expertise, but a real, demonstrated pull toward the space and the judgement to grow into leading it.

  • A strong interest in the nuances of the AI-assisted SDLC, and the conviction that tooling alone does not make engineers more potent. Adoption, practice and guardrails are what turn AI access into real leverage.

  • Kubernetes literacy, grounded in hands-on experience as an engineer, sufficient to reason about the estate and challenge the team's decisions.

  • AI fluency: candidates must be able to demonstrate practical, responsible use of AI in an engineering context and the ability to set team norms for it. We are looking for an active AI promoter who can reason about where AI adds leverage and where it is a liability in a compliance setting.

Title - PR & Marketing Executive

Location - Remote first but available for in person collaboration in Edinburgh or London

Aveni is redefining how financial institutions use AI. We build real, production-ready AI solutions that help financial services firms transform how they operate, manage risk and deliver better outcomes for their customers.

We’re looking for a PR & Marketing Executive to help build Aveni’s profile across the UK financial services market and support the delivery of our PR, communications and wider marketing activity.

This is a varied, hands-on role for someone who knows what makes a good story, enjoys building relationships with journalists and wants to develop their career at the intersection of AI, fintech and financial services.

 

The role

 

Working closely with the Head of PR & Communications, you’ll help tell Aveni’s story to the market, building relationships with journalists and industry influencers, identifying opportunities for Aveni to contribute to the conversation and securing relevant media coverage.

You’ll support the development of proactive PR campaigns, commentary and thought leadership around Aveni’s business priorities, product developments, customer successes and the wider issues shaping financial services.

The role goes beyond traditional media relations. You’ll also contribute to customer stories, executive and internal communications, events, awards, speaker opportunities, analyst relations and wider marketing campaigns.

You’ll work across Aveni, collaborating with Marketing, Sales, Product, Customer Success and senior leadership to make sure our communications are timely, consistent and aligned with our brand and market positioning.

 

What you’ll be doing

 

  • You’ll build and maintain relationships with journalists across UK business, financial services, fintech, compliance, risk and technology media, proactively pitching stories, commentary, interviews and contributed content.

  • You’ll support the development and delivery of PR campaigns around Aveni’s business priorities, product launches, research, customer stories and relevant market developments.

  • You’ll help run Aveni’s day-to-day press office, responding to journalist enquiries, identifying commentary opportunities, coordinating interviews and preparing briefing materials.

  • You’ll maintain our communications and editorial calendar across PR, thought leadership, research, webinars, awards, speaking opportunities and company announcements.

  • You’ll work with Sales and Customer Success to identify and develop compelling customer stories, case studies, testimonials and joint communications.

  • You’ll support internal communications, helping colleagues stay informed about company news, customer wins, product developments, events and media coverage.

  • You’ll work with Aveni’s senior leaders and subject matter experts to build their external profiles through LinkedIn content, commentary, talking points and other communications.

  • You’ll support our thought leadership programme, helping develop webinars, research reports, whitepapers and other content around the issues that matter to our market.

  • You’ll identify and coordinate relevant conference, panel, podcast and webinar speaking opportunities, as well as industry awards.

  • You’ll support our relationships with industry analysts and research organisations and help coordinate analyst briefings and materials.

  • You’ll work with the wider Marketing team to support conferences, roundtables, webinars and customer events.

 

What we’re looking for

 

  • You’ll have solid experience in PR, communications or a closely related role, with experience working in a B2B environment.

  • You’ll have experience dealing directly with journalists and proactively pitching stories and ideas.

  • You’ll be a strong writer and editor, comfortable producing press releases, pitches, commentary and other external communications.

  • You’ll have strong news judgement and be able to identify what makes a compelling story and how to tailor it for different audiences.

  • You’ll be confident communicating with journalists, senior stakeholders and external partners.

  • You’ll be able to take complex or technical subjects and turn them into clear, engaging communications.

  • You’ll be highly organised, with excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines and priorities at the same time.

  • You’ll understand the role PR and communications play in building brand awareness, reputation and supporting wider commercial objectives.

  • You’ll have a genuine interest in AI, fintech, financial services and the wider media agenda.

  • You’ll be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly and be confident building relationships across the business.

 

Nice to have

 

  • Experience working with UK financial services, fintech, compliance, risk, regulatory or technology media.

  • Experience within a PR agency and/or an in-house B2B communications role.

  • Existing relationships with journalists covering financial services, fintech, compliance, risk or related sectors.

  • Experience supporting events, awards, speaker programmes or analyst relations.

  • Familiarity with PR monitoring and media database platforms.

  • Experience using HubSpot or other marketing automation platforms.

Senior Product Manager, Core People Technology

Location: London | Work model: Hybrid | Reports to: Senior Manager, People Product

About the team

People Technology builds and runs the systems behind every hire, transfer, leave, pay change and offboard for our workforce across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt. Our mission is to make the operational backbone of People Operations invisible when it works — reliable, compliant, and scalable across dozens of markets — so our people teams can focus on people, not process. This role sits on the People Product team, working alongside Business Systems Analysts, engineers and delivery leadership to bring product thinking to one of our highest-volume, highest-consequence surfaces.

About the role

Core is the Workday and HR platform surface that nearly every People Operations process runs through — pay, leave, employment status, right to work, and multi-country compliance for a global workforce. Demand structurally exceeds capacity, and requests arrive from every direction without a shared shape. You'll be the first dedicated product manager for this space, responsible for turning that inbound chaos into a defensible, well-communicated plan — and, over time, for building the intake, frameworks and partnerships that let the space run on systems rather than on you.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role: you'll be shaping tickets and sizing work alongside analysts and engineers, not managing from above.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the prioritised order of work for Core — building a clear, ranked plan, explaining the reasoning behind it, and being explicit about what's being deferred and why

  • Turn vague or incomplete partner requests into documented problems, mapped current-state processes, and testable outcomes

  • Partner directly and regularly with People Operations, Compliance, Payroll, Total Rewards and Business Systems Analysts, including holding "not now" conversations without damaging the relationship

  • Work hands-on with analysts and engineers to shape, size, and write tickets, keeping an accurate and current picture of committed, shipped, and carried-over work

  • Build and evolve the operating model across the analyst and engineering pod — the mechanisms, documentation and intake processes that let the space run with less coordination overhead

  • Use AI tools to accelerate translation of messy, multi-format, multi-language inbound requests into structured requirements and plans, while applying clear judgment about what should never be automated (anything touching pay, leave, employment status or right to work)

  • Escalate proactively on statutory or audit exposure, cross-space dependencies, and any trade-off that would move a compliance date

  • Report progress and delivery against plan to partners and leadership, including clear communication when outcomes fall short

Requirements

  • Experience owning a product or systems area end-to-end, with real decision rights over scope and sequencing — not co-ownership of a feature

  • Hands-on background with Workday or a comparable HRIS as a product manager or technical program manager, with genuine understanding of configuration, business processes, and integrations

  • Demonstrated ability to prioritise when demand structurally exceeds capacity, including a repeatable method (not just instinct) for deciding what to do and communicating what won't get done

  • Proven delivery in ambiguous, fast-moving environments, comfortable starting when requirements are incomplete or undocumented

  • Experience translating a partner's requested solution into a well-defined problem, current-state understanding, and testable outcome

  • Strong collaboration skills across technical and non-technical stakeholders, including compliance, payroll, or other regulated/audit-exposed functions

  • Practical fluency with AI tools for requirements drafting, documentation, and structuring unstructured information, paired with sound judgment about where not to apply them

Why Deliveroo

Our mission is to transform the way you shop and eat, bringing the neighborhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops and riders. We are transforming the way the world eats and shops by making access to food and products more convenient and enjoyable. We give people the opportunity to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it.

We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of the most rapidly expanding industry in the world. We are still a small team, making a very large impact, looking to answer some of the most interesting questions out there. We move fast, value autonomy and ownership, and we are always looking for new ideas.

Workplace & Benefits

At Deliveroo we know that people are the heart of the business and we prioritise their welfare. Benefits differ by country, but we offer many benefits in areas including healthcare, well-being, parental leave, pensions, and generous annual leave allowances, including time off to support a charitable cause of your choice. Benefits are country-specific, please ask your recruiter for more information.

Diversity

At Deliveroo, we believe a great workplace is one that represents the world we live in and how beautifully diverse it can be. That means we have no judgement when it comes to any one of the things that make you who you are - your gender, race, sexuality, religion or a secret aversion to coriander. All you need is a passion for (most) food and a desire to be part of one of the fastest-growing businesses in a rapidly growing industry.

We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion in all aspects of our hiring process. Meet Siena

Siena is the The Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.

It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on.

The team

We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.

We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.

If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.

The role

Siena is building the intelligence layer for CX, and we're about to launch several products in quick succession. We are not looking for someone to execute a brief well. We are looking for the person whose taste the rest of the company gets measured against: someone who looks at a landing page and can't not have an opinion, who would rather kill a launch than ship something mediocre, and who has owned creative direction before, not just contributed to it.

If you need a creative director above you setting the vision, a team to delegate to on day one, or a slow, considered, one-project-at-a-time pace, stop reading now. This isn't that job.

If you're the person other designers already defer to on taste, continue.

This is a craft title. Not a headcount title.

You will ship personally for the first year and set the bar for everyone who comes after. Over time you will build a small internal agency, two to three people across design, motion, and content, that can brief, position, and launch without outside help.

  • Narrative and positioning across every launch - design as strategy, not decoration

  • Every artifact that goes to market: landing pages, launch video, decks, social

  • The design system, from v3 onward

  • The bar, full stop - if it ships under the Siena name, you made it or you signed off on it

What it takes to be in the room

  • Taste, above everything, and evidence you can defend it. Specific, defended opinions about what's good and why.

  • A track record of owning creative direction, not just contributing to it. Agency or in-house, brand refresh or full launch - you've been the person whose call was final, not the one waiting on notes.

  • Narrative thinking. Design as positioning. You should already have a point of view on how a brand like Siena should be positioned, not just how it should look.

  • AI as a working tool, not a threat to your taste. You've already built something with AI - an app, a prototype, a mockup - and you want to get technical enough to ship a landing page yourself within a year. Anti-AI is disqualifying.

  • Range that travels. Your background doesn't have to be SaaS. Fashion, art, consumer brand, editorial - what matters is whether your taste holds up somewhere new.

  • A pattern of shipping in chaos, not around it. Multiple launches in flight, feedback that moves in hours not weeks. If your best work happens on a slow, protected timeline, that's useful information - it's just not this role.

Why this is worth it

You're not joining a design team to fit into. You're setting the taste bar for a company that's about to be a lot more visible, a lot faster than most companies get that chance.

This is intense - real ownership, real launches, a founder team that reviews your work directly and moves at the pace you'd expect from that. It's also one of the rare creative seats where nothing you make gets diluted by committee before it ships.

If that sounds like the room you've been trying to get into, we want to talk to you.

If it sounds like too much scrutiny too fast, this isn't a knock on you - it just isn't this role.

Why Siena?

  • Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.

  • Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.

  • A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.

  • A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.

A ground-breaking & award-winning Construction Technology company; XYZ Reality are the creators of the world's first and only engineering-grade Augmented Reality solution, purpose-built for the construction industry. Not only have we created this technology, that sits within The Atom – a smart, site-safe headset and hardhat - but we implement it on major Mission Critical (Data Centres, Oil & Gas, Pharmaceutical, Aviation) projects, utilising the power of AR to ensure that all schemes are completed in line with the delivery timescales and budgets.

Overview

As Account Executive – Mission Critical, you will be directly responsible for driving new revenue through the development and execution of strategic territory and account plans within mission-critical construction sectors (data centres, pharma, healthcare, nuclear, semiconductor, and related industries).

Leveraging your deep construction and enterprise sales experience, you will identify, qualify, and close complex opportunities by solving customer challenges through the XYZ Reality platform. You will act as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders, articulating clear business value, ROI, and risk reduction while building long-term, influential partnerships across your accounts.

This role is focused on new account acquisition and strategic account expansion, managing sophisticated, multi-stakeholder sales cycles from initial engagement through contract negotiation, close, and post-sale alignment. You will carry annual and quarterly targets and operate as a core member of the revenue organization.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and Execute Account & Territory Strategy

  • Develop and execute strategic territory and account plans aligned to revenue targets and long-term growth objectives

  • Identify high-value target accounts and prioritize opportunities based on market potential, customer maturity, and strategic fit

  • Build and maintain accurate pipeline forecasts and revenue plans

Strategic Relationship Building

  • Build and expand executive-level relationships across assigned accounts, engaging stakeholders from site level through C-suite

  • Identify and develop decision-makers, champions, influencers, and economic buyers

  • Establish XYZ Reality as a strategic partner, not just a technology vendor

Consultative & Value-Based Selling

  • Lead with a consultative selling approach, deeply understanding customer challenges, delivery risk, and commercial drivers

  • Translate customer pain points into compelling business cases that clearly demonstrate value, ROI, and operational impact

  • Align XYZ Reality’s AR solution to customer objectives across safety, quality, schedule, and cost control

Manage Complex Sales Cycles

  • Own the end-to-end sales process: prospecting, qualification, solution alignment, commercial negotiation, and close

  • Navigate complex deal structures, including enterprise-level negotiations, procurement processes, and contractual requirements

  • Support and respond to RFPs / formal bid processes where required, partnering closely with internal stakeholders

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with Marketing, SDRs, Revenue Operations, Professional Services, and Delivery teams to drive new business and expansion

  • Partner internally to align technical solutions, services strategy, and commercial structures to customer needs

  • Ensure smooth handoff from sales to implementation and ongoing account success

Partner & Ecosystem Engagement

  • Collaborate with construction partners, consultants, and industry stakeholders to drive co-selling opportunities

  • Leverage partner relationships to strengthen account strategy and accelerate deal velocity

Market & Competitive Intelligence

  • Stay informed on industry trends, competitor activity, and market dynamics within mission-critical construction

  • Provide feedback to leadership on product positioning, customer insights, and evolving market needs

Sales Operations & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date records in Salesforce, including opportunities, forecasts, and next steps

  • Analyse sales data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for optimization

You Could Be a Strong Candidate If You Have:

  • Proven experience owning complex, enterprise sales cycles with annual quotas

  • Track record of closing 6-figure+ deals with multiple stakeholders and long decision cycles

  • Strong experience in value-based and solution selling, including account planning and strategic execution

  • Excellent communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences

  • CRM discipline and comfort operating in structured sales processes

The Ideal Candidate:

  • Experience selling into mission-critical construction environments (data centre, pharma, semiconductor, nuclear, oil & gas)

  • Background in construction technology, SaaS, or cloud-based solutions

  • Comfortable engaging senior executives while also operating on site and with delivery teams

  • Proactive, coachable, and energized by building long-term customer relationships

  • Willing and able to travel domestically and internationally for meetings and demos

About ARQ

ARQ is one of the fastest-growing fintechs in the world. Our mission is to redefine how people interact with money across borders, building the infrastructure to move value seamlessly. We’re still early in our journey, which means every person who joins shapes the future of our product, culture, and growth. If you’re excited by big challenges, global impact, and the chance to grow fast with a world-class team, ARQ is the place to do it.

What we're looking for

As a Backend Engineer, you’ll design, develop, and maintain scalable, secure, and high-performing backend systems that power our innovative products. You’ll collaborate with a talented team to create solutions that drive financial inclusion and transform the way people manage their money.

What you'll be doing

  • The work will focus on greenfield development and improvement of existing systems

  • Projects will include building REST APIs, engineering microservices and evolving a number of systems that our business depends on (e.g. card payments, treasury management, transactions booking, crypto liquidity)

  • Our technology stack is based predominantly on Java 25 on the backend with Postgres database

  • We rely on Spring Boot for quick and quality delivery

  • We have a pragmatic approach to develop our business logic, focusing on clean code, with emphasis on maintainability and fast turnaround with TDD, DDD and continuous integration & delivery

What you'll need

  • Demonstrable experience in Backend development, with fluency in Java

  • Bachelor's Degree (or above) in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or other Engineering / Science disciplines

  • Quick learner with an ambitious and results driven personality, with excellent communication skills (english fluency, verbal and written)

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and benefits

Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on.

Watch our showcase >

Read up on our $100m Series C

Learn more about our culture >

Which team will you be joining?

You’ll be joining the ProdSec/AppSec team to help build the entire product security surface for a company processing payments at scale: threat modelling, security review, compliance, incident escalation, and the multi-year AppSec roadmap. You'd be the second hire, and the person that function finally gets to share the work with.

This is a hands-on delivery role, and a genuinely formative one. You’ll help set the security strategy and architecture; you take real ownership of the work that turns it into reality, reviews, research, automation, and the day-to-day partnership with engineering teams. You'll have a clear direction to work within and someone senior to learn from, while still owning your projects end to end.

Security at Primer sits close to the engineering teams it protects rather than off to one side, so you'll spend real time embedded with the people building Cloud, Infra, and product. For someone who wants to go deep in product security with room to grow, there are few better seats than being the second engineer in a function that's only now scaling.

 

What will you be doing?

  • Running security reviews and threat modelling on features and systems across Primer's product, and turning findings into clear, actionable guidance for the teams shipping them

  • Independently planning and delivering your own security projects, from initial design through to rollout

  • Building tooling and automation that makes future reviews faster and cheaper to run

  • Coordinating penetration testing and tracking remediation through to closure

  • Supporting the recurring compliance work (SOC2, PCI), including evidence collection and remediation tracking against fixed audit windows

  • Contributing to AppSec roadmap initiatives across areas like application threats, AI security, supply chain security, and ASPM

  • Picking up proactive security work, threat research and hands-on investigation, that a one-person function has never had the capacity for

  • Working alongside Cloud, Infra, and GRC on the security aspects of their projects

 

What we're looking for

  • Working experience in product or application security: you've done security reviews or threat modelling and can spot the risks that matter

  • The ability to read and write code, not just review it. You're comfortable building small tools and automation rather than only filing findings

  • Sound judgement about risk. You can weigh a real threat against a theoretical one and explain your reasoning clearly

  • The ability to plan and deliver your own work independently once you understand the direction, while knowing when to pull in the senior engineer

  • Clear communication with engineers who aren't security specialists, since most of your impact lands through their work

Nice to have:

  • Exposure to compliance frameworks like SOC2 or PCI, or genuine appetite to learn them

  • Background in payments, fintech, or another regulated, high-stakes domain

  • Interest in areas like supply chain security, detection engineering, or AI security

 

You may not like it here

  • It's remote-first and high autonomy. You'll get direction, but nobody checks your progress daily. If you need close structure, this will be uncomfortable

  • You'll move between proactive project work and reactive BAU, and priorities will shift as audits and incidents land. Tolerating that change is part of the role.

✅ A typical interview process

  • An initial intro call with a Talent Partner

  • An interview with the Hiring Manager

  • Challenge Stage - Contextualised to the role

  • A final, values-alignment interview

What's the culture like at Primer?


We're building a culture where people can do their best work and be proud of the impact they have. You'll be working with people who are mission-driven, smart, and reflective, and who are genuinely invested in building exceptional products and delivering success for our merchants.

We work remotely, and have done since day one. We believe that building a successful, profitable company goes beyond proximity. We invest in our relationships through great remote working practices and thoughtfully designed face-to-face time, including workations, our annual company retreat, and access to co-working spaces across most major cities.

The work is challenging. Scaleups are a challenge, and building category-defining products is a challenge. But there's a meaningful difference between a challenge and a struggle. At Primer, the right challenge comes with the right support: strong onboarding, a collaborative environment, and a team that is genuinely invested in your success. It's never something you face alone.

Don’t meet every single requirement?

Role Overview

The Senior Risk Manager (Financial Risk) will provide an independent second line of defence oversight, challenge and assurance over the Firm's financial risk profile, with a particular focus on liquidity risk, market risk and counterparty credit risk. You will play a key role in ensuring the ICARA process and Wind-Down Plan are robust, appropriately challenged and effectively embedded, working closely with Treasury, Trading and Finance first line teams. This role requires deep technical expertise in financial risk management, prudential regulation and capital/liquidity adequacy within an FCA-regulated investment firm.

What you'll do

  • Provide independent second line oversight, challenge and assurance over the Firm's liquidity risk, market risk and counterparty credit risk exposures, ensuring these remain within Board-approved risk appetite.

  • Own and continuously enhance the 2LOD monitoring framework for liquidity risk, covering funding risk, market liquidity risk, intra-day liquidity risk, settlement risk, foreign currency position risk and liquidity concentration risk.

  • Understand and challenge Group wide market risk exposures including interest rate risk, FX risk, trading risk, asset concentration risk and the Firm's exposure to extreme market events.

  • Oversee and challenge the Firm's counterparty credit risk framework, including credit processing and aggregation risk, credit appetite and policy, and the identification of emerging credit risks and adverse counterparty trends.

  • Provide second line input into the ICARA process, ensuring liquidity adequacy and capital adequacy risks are appropriately identified, quantified and stressed, and providing credible challenge to first line methodologies and assumptions.

  • Ensure the Wind-Down Plan is fit for purpose, appropriately triggered via early warning indicators, and regularly tested, challenged and updated in line with regulatory expectations.

  • Oversee and challenge liquidity stress testing and scenario analysis, including severe but plausible and reverse stress test scenarios, to assess resilience under stressed conditions.

  • Review and challenge the effectiveness of first line risk management performed by Treasury and intr-Group Trading entities/ functions, including the design of liquidity buffers, trading limits and counterparty credit limits.

  • Support the identification and enhancement of quantitative and qualitative risk appetite measures for financial risk, ensuring appropriate tracking, escalation and remediation of breaches.

  • Deliver periodic independent 2LOD assurance through thematic reviews and deep dives into Treasury operations and counterparty exposure management.

  • Maintain oversight of relevant financial risk registers, ensuring risks are appropriately identified, assessed and tracked to resolution.

  • Provide second line risk review and challenge for new products, trading venues, asset classes and strategic initiatives that could materially affect the Firm's liquidity, market or counterparty credit risk profile.

  • Support ongoing monitoring of early warning indicators and contribute to Recovery and Resolution planning where relevant.

  • Foster a healthy risk culture, promoting risk management as a universal responsibility and encouraging open, transparent discussion of financial risk issues without fear of retaliation.

What you need to have

  • Extensive experience in liquidity risk, market risk and/or counterparty credit risk management, ideally within an FCA-regulated investment firm, broker or trading platform.

  • Strong working knowledge of the FCA's MIFIDPRU framework, including the ICARA process, liquidity adequacy assessment and Wind-Down Planning.

  • Solid understanding of Treasury functions, including funding, liquidity buffer management and collateral management.

  • Understanding of counterparty credit risk assessment methodologies, including exposure aggregation, credit appetite setting and counterparty due diligence.

  • Proven second line of defence experience, with the ability to provide credible, evidence-based challenge to first line stakeholders including Treasury, Trading and Finance.

  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including experience of stress testing and scenario analysis.

  • Experience with Recovery and Resolution Planning is highly desirable.

data.description:
Location: Remote in Europe

 

About Nivoda 🚀

Nivoda is a rapidly scaling global B2B diamond and gemstone marketplace connecting jewellery retailers with competitive, high-quality suppliers worldwide. Processing $300M+ in annual transactions and operating across multiple regions, Nivoda is transforming a $350B industry that has historically been slow to modernise.

Our platform gives businesses of all sizes, from independent jewellers to major retail chains access to the world's best diamond and gemstone inventory, without the traditional barriers of capital, geography, or information asymmetry.

 

Our Mission 🎯

Diamond and gemstone trading has long been plagued by inefficiency, opacity, and exclusivity. Nivoda was built to change that - to democratise access and empower every business, regardless of size or location, to buy and sell with confidence. Independent jewellers are at the heart of this mission. They deserve the same access to quality, pricing, and selection as the biggest players in the industry. That's exactly what we give them.

 

About the Role 🤔

Conversion is one of the three chokepoints in our revenue organisation. Customers arrive, take the demo, go through KYC, and too many stall before the first purchase, or buy once and never come back. The second purchase is where the product becomes sticky, and getting a merchant there is the hardest 60 days of their life with us.

Fixing that takes two things, and this role owns both. Reps who know the product, the pricing and the playbook cold. And a conversion funnel that is measured, scored and coached rather than hoped for.

 

Function one: enablement

Training and standards

  • Make sure every rep is up to spec and trained, and keep them there.

  • Own the theoretical onboarding of every new rep, SDR, AE and AM alike: what Nivoda sells, to whom, at what price, and how.

  • Set what "up to spec" means for each role and hold the bar.

Documentation and materials

  • Own the product material for every line of business: how it works, who it is for, pricing, take rate and best practice.

  • Keep it current. A rep should never be the last person to find out something changed.

The channel to marketing

  • Act as the link between marketing and the front line. Every campaign is known to the reps in advance, socialised at the all-hands before it lands, not discovered from a customer.

The channel to product

  • Translate the product roadmap into enablement. You do not decide the roadmap. You turn it into what to sell, to whom, and when.

  • When something ships, the reps already know what it is and how to position it.

Function two: conversion

Conversion rests on two things, and this role owns both: the call, and the KYC. A brilliant call that dies in KYC converts nothing, and a clean KYC on a badly run call never gets there.

Call scoring

  • Build the scoring rubrics with the team managers, so the standard is one both sides recognise.

  • Run transcript review and scoring at volume, using Claude to do it.

  • Send the reports out every week, to everyone.

data.description:
About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Sustainability Team 👋

At Trainline, environmental sustainability sits at the heart of what we do. Through our technology and data, we make rail travel easier and help people choose more sustainable ways to get around. Rail already offers a far greener alternative to flying or driving, and we believe we have a genuine role to play in supporting the wider industry, businesses and governments to hit their own emissions targets. We were one of the first tech companies to have science-based net zero targets officially validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), committing to net zero by 2040 and a 55% reduction in scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030.

This role sits within our sustainability team, working closely with our Company Secretary and Director of Sustainability. You'll take the lead on embedding our emissions data platform, driving supplier engagement on our net-zero journey, and acting as an ambassador for corporate sustainability both inside and outside the business. You'll collaborate closely with teams across Trainline who own supplier relationships and data, as well as with senior stakeholders, to keep momentum going on one of our most important long-term commitments.

In this role as the Senior Corporate Sustainability Manager, you will...🚄

  • Own the ongoing delivery of our SBTi-validated emissions reduction strategy, with a strong focus on supplier engagement and reducing scope 3 emissions

  • Lead the continued rollout and adoption of Watershed, our GHG data platform, ensuring it is fully embedded ahead of the financial year reporting cycle

  • Own the ongoing implementation and adoption of Watershed, our GHG data collection platform, ensuring it is fully embedded ahead of the financial year reporting cycle

  • Be the ambassador for corporate sustainability, confidently presenting our progress and priorities to audiences across the business and building genuine engagement with the topic

  • Build strong working relationships with the teams who own supplier relationships

  • Support the development of frameworks for sustainability-linked disclosure requirements and help put them into action

  • Identify and lead workstreams that improve our ESG ratings over time

  • Help shape how we measure and report on emerging areas, such as the emissions impact of AI, where established methodologies don't yet exist

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • Experience driving a corporate sustainability agenda forward, ideally within a progressive or tech-led organisation

  • A solid background implementing science-based target reduction plans or similar programmes, ideally with hands-on experience of a GHG data platform such as Watershed

  • Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence and engage stakeholders across a business, from data owners to senior leadership

  • Confidence presenting to and engaging audiences, both internally and externally, on sustainability progress and priorities

  • A curious, open-minded approach to new tools and ways of working, including AI.

  • Experience leading change or transformation initiatives while balancing long-term goals with short-term delivery

More information:

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 

  • 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

  • ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

  • 🤝  Travel Together - We're one team 

  • ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor!

About the team

SumUp is best known for helping small businesses get paid — our Consumer tribe builds the other half of that story. We make SumUp Consumer, the wallet app that lets everyday consumers pay SumUp merchants with a tap, send money to friends, track their spending and earn loyalty rewards along the way.

As we grow SumUp Consumer across new markets and features, we need sharp, reliable insight into how people discover, adopt and use the product — and how that behaviour translates into sustainable commercial growth. This includes understanding our acquisition funnel, improving activation and conversion, increasing customer value, and reducing churn.

We're looking for a Product Data Analyst to join the Consumer tribe and become the analytical partner for SumUp Consumer. You'll work closely with Product Managers, Designers and Engineers, alongside our Analytics Engineering team, to understand customer behaviour, shape product strategy, and connect product performance to business outcomes.

You'll help answer questions such as:

  • Which acquisition channels and customer segments generate the strongest long-term value?
  • Where do customers drop out of the journey from acquisition to activation?
  • What drives repeat usage, retention and churn?
  • Which product changes improve conversion, customer value or commercial performance?
  • How should we prioritise product investments across markets and customer segments?

If you're motivated by meaningful analytical work, enjoy translating complexity into clarity, and want to see your insights directly influence both product decisions and commercial outcomes, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Analyse customer behaviour and product performance across the full consumer lifecycle — from acquisition and activation through engagement, retention, churn and reactivation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve conversion, customer value and sustainable growth using funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analytics.
  • Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers and Data teams to ensure decisions are grounded in robust analysis, customer insight and commercial understanding.
  • Evaluate the performance of customer segments, markets, channels and product journeys, helping the team understand where growth opportunities and commercial trade-offs exist.
  • Support decisions that improve key business outcomes, such as activation, conversion, repeat usage, retention, churn, customer lifetime value and revenue-related metrics.
  • Conduct exploratory analysis to answer product and business questions, translating complex data into clear, commercially relevant recommendations.
  • Define, monitor and communicate core SumUp Consumer KPIs, covering acquisition, activation, engagement, conversion, retention, churn and customer value.
  • Design, execute and analyse A/B tests and product experiments, assessing both customer impact and commercial impact.
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that stakeholders actively use, proactively surfacing trends, anomalies, performance risks and growth opportunities.
  • Help Product Managers assess the expected impact of opportunities and evaluate whether product investments are delivering the intended customer and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Analytics Engineering to ensure KPI definitions, business logic and product instrumentation are accurate, scalable and trusted.
  • Bring a curious eye to AI and machine learning techniques, including LLM-assisted analysis, to speed up insight generation, customer understanding and product measurement.

You'll be great for this role if…

  • You have strong SQL skills and are comfortable querying, analysing and validating data in a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or similar.
  • You have hands-on experience with product analytics techniques such as funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analysis.
  • You understand the commercial drivers of a digital product, including customer acquisition, conversion, activation, retention, churn and customer lifetime value.
  • You can connect customer behaviour and product performance to business outcomes, and use data to identify growth opportunities and inform prioritisation.
  • You've worked on A/B tests or product experiments, with a solid grounding in the statistics behind them.
  • You're proficient in a visualisation tool such as Looker, Tableau or Power BI, with a track record of building dashboards that stakeholders actually use.
  • You can translate ambiguous product or business questions into structured analysis, and explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
  • You're comfortable assessing trade-offs, challenging assumptions and making recommendations based on evidence.
  • You're curious about how AI and emerging techniques can improve product measurement, experimentation, customer understanding and commercial decision-making.
  • You're comfortable managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders, with strong prioritisation and a proactive communication style.

This role does not support Visa sponsorship and candidates must have the right to work in the UK.

Why you should join SumUp

🌎 Opportunity to work with a truly global, multicultural team from our central London Bridge location, wrapped in historic charm and modern flair. This involves an office-first setup

🌈 Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: be part of a workplace that values and promotes diversity, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone's perspectives are respected and embraced

🚀 Enrolment onto our Virtual Stock Option programme: you will own a stake in SumUp's future success

🏖 Generous time off: enjoy 28 days of paid leave, plus bank holidays and special leaves

📚 A dedicated annual L&D budget for attending conferences and/or advancing your career through further education

🏥 Health matters: private health insurance, including optical and dental

🚗 Life made easier: salary-sacrifice commuter benefits via Gogeta

💼 Financial security: retirement scheme (SumUp matches 7% when you contribute 5%)

🛡 Peace of mind: life insurance from MetLife for 2× your salary

🌴 Break4me: 1-month sabbatical after 3 years of service

🔗 Referral Bonus: earn additional rewards by referring talented individuals to join the SumUp team

About SumUp

Be empowered to do more that matters.

At SumUp, we're on a mission to empower small businesses across the globe by providing simple and affordable tools that allow them to thrive. Today, over 4 million businesses in 37 markets rely on SumUp as their financial partner to manage payments, finance and customer relationships.

Our commitment to small businesses is reflected in our diverse team of over 3,000 SumUppers from over 90 nationalities, united by global collaboration and an innovative mindset. Our core values lay the foundation for who we are and what we stand for, shaping our work culture and driving our success. We foster inclusivity and a continuous learning culture, providing a safe space for personal and professional growth. Our differences make us unique and strong as we strive to create an environment where everyone belongs and feels supported, no matter how they identify.

SumUp is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer, actively seeking and embracing diversity in our workforce. We don't make hiring or employment decisions based on race, colour, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age or any other basis protected by applicable laws or prohibited by company policy. Our commitment extends beyond recruitment to creating a safe and respectful workplace where harassment of any form is strictly prohibited. Discover more about our culture and opportunities on our careers website, and follow our journey on LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok.

HackerOne is a global leader in Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). The HackerOne Platform unites agentic AI solutions with the ingenuity of the world’s largest community of security researchers to continuously discover, validate, prioritize, and remediate exposures across code, cloud, and AI systems. Through solutions like bug bounty, vulnerability disclosure, agentic pentesting, AI red teaming, and code security, HackerOne delivers measurable, continuous reduction of cyber risk for enterprises. Industry leaders, including Anthropic, Crypto.com, General Motors, Goldman Sachs, Lufthansa, Uber, UK Ministry of Defence, and the U.S. Department of Defense, trust HackerOne to safeguard their digital ecosystems. HackerOne was recognized in Gartner’s Emerging Tech Impact Radar: AI Cybersecurity Ecosystem report for its leadership in AI Security Testing and has been named a Most Loved Workplace for Young Professionals (2024).

HackerOne is at a pivotal inflection point in the security industry. Offensive security is no longer optional – it is the standard for forward-thinking companies that want to build trust and resilience in a world where AI-driven innovation and adversaries are moving faster than ever. With the industry shifting, HackerOne stands apart: we combine the ingenuity of the largest security research community with a best-in-class AI-powered platform, trusted by the world’s top organizations.

HackerOne Values

HackerOne is dedicated to fostering a strong and inclusive culture. HackerOne is Customer Obsessed and prioritizes customer outcomes in our decisions and actions. We Default to Disclosure by operating with transparency and integrity, ensuring trust and accountability. Employees, researchers, customers, and partners Win Together by fostering empowerment, inclusion, respect, and accountability.

Senior Security Engineer, Detection and Response

Remote Location: Austin TX, Seattle, WA, Washington, DC, San Francisco, CA, Boston, MA

Position Summary

At HackerOne, we’re rebuilding our Detection & Response function with an AI-first approach—focused on engineering, not just triage. As a Senior Security Engineer, you will design and deliver detection and response capabilities that protect a modern, cloud-native environment by writing code, building AI-powered tooling, and automating workflows end-to-end.

This role operates across the full detection lifecycle—from identifying gaps in observability to shipping high-signal detections and leading incident response when it matters most. You’ll help scale what a small team can accomplish by embedding automation, intelligence, and AI into how we detect and respond to threats.

At HackerOne, we embrace a Flexible Work approach that gives us the freedom to do our best work while also fostering the connections and community that make us stronger. Reflecting this philosophy, this is a remote role targeted for candidates within ~50 miles of Austin TX, Seattle, WA, Washington, DC, San Francisco, CA, or Boston, MA . We believe this balance of proximity and flexibility gives Hackeronies the chance to occasionally come together – fostering collaboration, connection, and in-person moments that enrich our culture – while still preserving the benefits of remote work.

What You Will Do

Success in the Senior Security Engineer role will be accomplished by delivering on the responsibilities below in alignment with the Values and Principles that define how we work at HackerOne:

  • Design, build, and maintain detection-as-code capabilities across cloud infrastructure, SaaS applications, endpoints, and identity systems, improving coverage and signal quality through Data-Driven Decision Making

  • Partner cross-functionally with engineering and platform teams to expand logging, improve observability, and embed detection capabilities into the development lifecycle

  • Continuously improve detection quality by analyzing alert performance, tuning for signal, and building feedback loops between incidents and detections using Data-Driven Decision Making

  • Proactively identify gaps in visibility or coverage and translate ambiguous problem spaces into concrete detection and response solutions through First Principles Problem Solving

  • Adapt quickly to evolving threats, tools, and priorities, helping the team maintain momentum and effectiveness through Change Agility

Minimum Qualifications  

  • 5+ years of experience in detection and response, security engineering, or software engineering with a security focus

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals with proficiency in Python, Go, Ruby, or similar languages, and experience working in production codebases

  • Hands-on experience with cloud environments (AWS preferred), including services such as CloudTrail, GuardDuty, and VPC flow logs

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building AI/LLM-powered security tooling or applying AI to detection, triage, or investigation workflows

We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

If you don’t choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself then, choose the challenge, choose Heidi.

The role

We are hiring a Clinical Trials Lead to own the commercial work that follows. You will develop Heidi’s view of the market, identify the strongest entry point, build senior relationships across the industry, secure early customers and shape a repeatable route to market. Your knowledge of clinical trials will inform and shape what Heidi builds.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates like a founder. You will make the calls, open the doors, write the proposal, run the meeting and stay accountable after the contract is signed. As the business proves itself, the role can grow into broader ownership of Heidi’s clinical trials business.

What you’ll do

  • Develop the market thesis. Map the clinical trials ecosystem, test the most valuable opportunities and recommend where Heidi should focus its time and capital.

  • Lead customer development. Build direct relationships with senior decision makers across sponsors, biotechnology companies, CROs, sites and health systems. Conduct the outreach yourself and turn conversations into qualified opportunities.

  • Own early commercial outcomes. Build the pipeline, secure design partners and paid programmes, and own early revenue. Define the measures that show whether the business is gaining traction.

  • Shape the proposition. Turn buyer needs into a clear commercial offer, including target customer, value proposition, pricing, packaging and proof of value.

  • Inform what Heidi builds. Bring evidence from customers and clinical trials workflows to the product lead. Help the team choose problems worth solving while the product lead retains ownership of product strategy and delivery.

  • Navigate the buying process. Understand how life sciences organisations evaluate vendors, allocate budgets, manage procurement and compliance, and move from pilot to broader deployment.

  • Build the delivery model. Work with product, engineering, clinical, legal and implementation colleagues to make early programmes successful and increasingly repeatable.

  • Create the route to scale. Determine which partnerships, channels, proof points and team capabilities are required to grow beyond founder-led selling.

  • Represent Heidi. Build Heidi’s credibility with customers, partners and industry networks through thoughtful engagement and useful domain expertise.

What you’ll need

The strongest candidates will combine deep clinical trials knowledge with a record of creating commercial value. We expect the following experience.

  • Deep experience in the clinical trials industry through a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company, CRO, trial technology business, research network or closely related organisation.

  • A strong understanding of how clinical trials are funded, sold, bought and delivered, including the incentives and constraints faced by sponsors, CROs and research sites.

  • A record of building revenue, partnerships, a business line or a company in the sector. You can show what you personally originated and how it performed.

  • Senior commercial credibility. You can open a conversation with an industry executive, diagnose the underlying business problem and move the relationship towards a concrete commitment.

  • The judgement to operate in a regulated environment while respecting Good Clinical Practice, patient consent, privacy and data integrity.

  • The independence to create structure, make decisions and produce results without an established playbook or a large supporting team.

Additional strengths

  • Experience as a founder, early executive or leader who created a new clinical trials business or commercial proposition.

  • A strong network across pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology companies, CROs, research sites, health systems, investigators or patient organisations.

  • Experience across more than one side of the ecosystem, such as sponsor and site, CRO and technology, or clinical practice and commercial delivery.

  • Experience selling enterprise software, technology enabled services, recruitment programmes or data products to life sciences organisations.

  • Product fluency and the ability to turn market evidence into useful guidance for product and engineering teams.

  • Familiarity with clinical research systems such as CTMS, EDC, eConsent, ePRO, trial registries and EHR or EMR integrations.

  • A clinical or scientific qualification. This can strengthen your credibility, but it is not a substitute for commercial results.

  • Experience with Australian, UK or comparable clinical research markets.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who’ve felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you’re doing the defining work of your career.

We take care of you.

We offer comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a £100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a £500 home office budget, a £700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to £7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

About Mirakl:

Founded in 2012, Mirakl has been at the forefront of marketplace innovation, empowering every business to compete in the platform economy.

Today, Mirakl's operating system combines an enterprise marketplace solution (Mirakl Platform) that enables retailers and B2B organizations to launch, scale, and operate marketplaces and dropship, AI-powered multichannel selling (Mirakl Connect), retail media (Mirakl Ads) and an agentic commerce infrastructure (Mirakl Nexus).

With dual headquarters in Boston and Paris, Mirakl helps a global ecosystem of 450+ marketplaces (B2C and B2B) and a network of over 100k third-party marketplace sellers. Brands like Macy's, Decathlon, Carrefour, Asos, and Airbus Helicopters use Mirakl to grow their businesses in new and remarkable ways.

For more information: www.mirakl.com.

Mirakl in Numbers:

  • 🗓️ Founded in 2012 | Member of French Tech Next40
  • 👥 750+ employees in 9 offices worldwide: Paris, Barcelona, Bordeaux, Boston, London, Munich, New York, Sydney, Tokyo
  • 🇫🇷 350+ Mirakl Tech teams members mainly based in France
  • ⚙️ 5 Saas Solutions

Our Values:

Working at Mirakl means accelerating your career alongside ambitious, passionate, and supportive colleagues. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.

Our 5 values guide how we collaborate:

  • 💡 Work Hard Together: Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success
  • 🏆 Get Things Done:  We prioritize action and efficiency for impactful results
